You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is her jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: Assess the jacket’s front closure itself by comparing corresponding visible portions in SOURCE and EDITED. Full achievement requires the front panels to meet along the closure with no visible opening remaining. Count partial fulfillment only where corresponding visible portions show the panels have moved together toward closure while an opening remains. Assign zero only when corresponding closure portions are sufficiently visible and show no movement of the panels toward one another relative to SOURCE. If the closure or corresponding portions are obscured, or pose and drape prevent reliable comparison, treat the observation as unresolved rather than inferring zero or progress.
node.binding: Compare the original jacket on the woman in SOURCE with that same jacket in EDITED. Compare corresponding visible portions of the jacket closure, not the overall silhouette or how the jacket hangs. A changed pose or drape alone is not evidence of closure progress. If corresponding closure portions are not sufficiently visible for reliable comparison, use insufficient evidence.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: Corresponding portions of the closure are sufficiently visible in SOURCE and EDITED for comparison, and show no visible movement of the front panels toward one another. Do not assign zero from an open-looking silhouette, pose change, or drape; if the closure cannot be reliably compared, leave fulfillment unresolved.
node.half_when: Corresponding visible portions show the front panels moved together toward closure, but a visible opening remains. If pose, drape, or occlusion makes panel movement indeterminate, leave fulfillment unresolved rather than assigning partial fulfillment.
node.full_when: The jacket’s front panels meet along the visible closure, with no visible opening remaining; corresponding closure portions are sufficiently visible to establish this endpoint.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front closure is visible in SOURCE, but in EDITED she has turned and the jacket is swinging outward, obscuring the corresponding closure portions. The changed pose and drape do not establish whether the panels moved toward closure, so progress cannot be reliably assessed.

Otherwise retain unresolved. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
